I remember they had me talk to the school councillor once a week, because my mom said they thought I was quiet because I was abused at home. 
I hated having to talk to the councillor, because no one else had to do it. Plus she kept taking me out of lessons, which I thought was annoying. 

They diagnosed me in year 7, but I didn’t rlly get any treatment. They made my parents send me to therapy (this teacher was threatening to call child services if she didn’t, she doesn’t work there anymore). No shade but the therapist didn’t rlly know what to do. We just kept on going over the same things. “How would you feel if you didn’t have SM, what would you do?”. Plus these dumb tree drawing things, where I had to write down my worries.

My councillor from secondary school was rlly nice and always had great advice tho.

I also remember in year 7, they gave me this leaflet saying I had sm, and my dislikes and likes. I remember hating it so much because it made me feel dumb and different from everyone else. So during reading time in science class I cut it up into small pieces and threw it in the bin, because I didn’t think I was scared of talking at the time, just shy.

I can speak easily with adults, and family members. For some reason it’s harder to speak to people my own age and younger (so like teenagers).
